Japan’s minimum wage averages JPY 1,177 an hour after the fiscal 2026 revision, up JPY 56 (about 5%) from JPY 1,121. Each of the 47 prefectures sets its own rate, from JPY 1,085 in Miyazaki to JPY 1,280 in Tokyo, and the new rates take effect between 1 October and 2 December 2026.

Japan does not have a single national minimum wage. Each prefecture sets its own rate based on local economic conditions, cost of living and labour market dynamics, following a guideline from the Central Minimum Wages Council. On top of the regional minimums, some industries have specific minimum wages that apply when they are higher than the prefectural rate.

Exclusive, non-exclusive, white-label, and value-added arrangements give the reseller different levels of market access and control.

The parties must also decide who controls the customer relationship. For example, the reseller may own the commercial relationship while the vendor provides technical support. Alternatively, the reseller may bring in the sale while the vendor contracts directly with the customer. The latter arrangement may function more like a referral relationship.

A sales agent acts on the vendor's behalf under the authority granted by the agency arrangement. The vendor commonly enters the customer contract and controls the sale terms. A referral partner has a narrower role. It introduces a potential customer and may receive a fee if the vendor completes the sale, but it does not normally resell the product.

The contract should describe authority precisely. It should say whether the partner can accept orders, make warranties, negotiate customer terms, or bind the vendor. This reduces the risk that marketing conduct creates expectations beyond the intended relationship.

An original equipment manufacturer, or OEM, arrangement can overlap with white-label and VAR models. In a software relationship, the reseller may embed or rebrand the vendor's technology as part of a larger product. That arrangement requires detailed licensing, integration, quality-control, and ownership terms.

. An attorney can identify gaps, align reseller and customer-facing documents, and draft or revise terms for the specific product, sales model, and governing law. Responses typically arrive within a day.

A bottom-up structure allows customer terms to result from individual negotiations. It can accommodate large customers, but it increases review costs and creates a risk that the reseller promises warranties, indemnities, service levels, or liability terms the vendor has not accepted. The reseller agreement should identify which deviations require vendor approval.

White-label and OEM arrangements need additional detail. Address permitted rebranding, technical integration, documentation, quality control, customer disclosures, ownership of embedded components, and responsibility for implementation and training. If the reseller bundles separate professional services, those services can be governed by a separate customer agreement.

A requested three-party agreement among the vendor, reseller, and customer requires careful drafting. It can blur responsibility and expose the parties to inconsistent warranties or overlapping liability. Alternatives include direct vendor-customer terms combined with a separate reseller services agreement, or a referral model in which the vendor controls the customer contract.

Then compare the reseller agreement with purchase orders, price schedules, customer terms, service levels, privacy documents, and marketing materials. A well-drafted reseller agreement can still fail operationally if sales teams use inconsistent documents. Definitions should also remain consistent, particularly for customer, end user, product, territory, net revenue, renewal, and support.

A selling agreement is a contract governing the sale of goods, services, or another asset. Depending on the transaction, it may identify the item sold, price, payment method, delivery, acceptance, warranties, and remedies. A reseller agreement is more specialized because it establishes an ongoing right to resell another party's offerings to additional customers.

A value-added reseller adds services, features, hardware, or other enhancements to the original product before selling a broader solution. A standard reseller may sell the offering substantially as provided. Because a VAR creates additional deliverables, its contract needs clearer boundaries for implementation work, added warranties, ownership, and responsibility when the combined solution fails.

A distribution agreement authorizes a distributor to acquire and supply products within an agreed channel or territory. It helps the parties control purchasing, inventory, delivery, marketing, pricing procedures, and downstream sales. Unlike some direct reseller arrangements, a distributor may primarily supply retailers or resellers rather than sell each product to the ultimate end user.

A reseller can rebrand a product only when the agreement grants that right. White-label and OEM arrangements commonly permit approved rebranding, while ordinary reseller appointments may require the vendor's marks. The contract should specify permitted names, trademark licenses, approval rights, attribution, packaging, domain names, and what happens to branded materials when the relationship ends.

The minimum wage in Japan is established and regulated primarily by the Minimum Wage Act (Act No. 137 of 1959, as amended), which mandates employers to pay workers at least the prescribed minimum wage rate to ensure basic livelihoods and fair labor conditions.
Japan employs a decentralized approach to minimum wage determination through 47 Prefectural Minimum Wages Councils, each tasked with investigating local conditions and recommending regional

In annual deliberations, councils evaluate adjustments based on statutory factors including living expenses required for a healthy and cultural livelihood, regional wage levels, productivity, and enterprises' capacity to pay, with particular attention to the viability of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) that dominate Japan's economy.
The emphasis on SME burdens reflects Japan's economic structure, where such firms employ over 70% of the workforce and face varying regional competitiveness.

再販・ホワイトラベル.quote: Reseller Agreement: Key Terms, Types, and Templates

A reseller agreement defines how a vendor and reseller will market, sell, support, and profit from products or services. Understanding the available models and essential clauses helps you prevent pricing, customer, and intellectual property disputes.
A reseller agreement should identify the products, territory, customers, pricing structure, order process, branding rights, and support duties.
Exclusive, non-exclusive, white-label, and value-added arrangements give the reseller different levels of market access and control.
What Is a Reseller Agreement?

A reseller agreement is a contract between a supplier, commonly called the vendor, and a business authorized to resell the vendor's products or services. The reseller normally sells to end customers as a principal rather than merely introducing leads or acting in the vendor's name. The contract establishes what the reseller may sell, where it may sell, and under what conditions.

The parties must also decide who controls the customer relationship. For example, the reseller may own the commercial relationship while the vendor provides technical support. Alternatively, the reseller may bring in the sale while the vendor contracts directly with the customer. The latter arrangement may function more like a referral relationship.

The written terms should match actual operations. Calling a party a reseller will not resolve inconsistent billing, sales, or support practices. If the reseller also runs joint promotions, a separate or integrated
Reseller, Distributor, Agent, and Referral Partner Roles

Business teams sometimes use reseller and distributor interchangeably, but the intended role matters more than the label. A reseller usually purchases or obtains rights to a product and sells directly to end customers. A distributor may occupy an earlier position in the supply chain and supply multiple resellers. Both may set customer-facing terms within limits established by the vendor.
May sell to resellers rather than end users
Types of Reseller Agreements Compared

The right model depends on the vendor's channel strategy, the reseller's investment, and the amount of control each party needs. A reseller investing in local staff, training, or localization may seek exclusivity. A vendor prioritizing broad market coverage may prefer several non-exclusive resellers.
One reseller receives defined rights in a region, industry, or customer segment
Vendor may appoint other resellers or sell directly
Reseller sells under its own branding
Customer-facing support is often assigned to the reseller
Reseller adds services, features, hardware, or integrations
Reseller commonly supports its added components

A value-added reseller, or VAR, does more than resell the original offering. It might provide implementation, configuration, account management, training, or an integrated technology solution. The agreement should identify who owns newly created materials, configurations, and modifications. It should also distinguish support for the vendor's product from support for the reseller's added services.

An original equipment manufacturer, or OEM, arrangement can overlap with white-label and VAR models. In a software relationship, the reseller may embed or rebrand the vendor's technology as part of a larger product. That arrangement requires detailed licensing, integration, quality-control, and ownership terms.
What a Reseller Agreement Template Should Include

A reseller agreement template should function as a clause checklist, not as a finished contract. Start by documenting the parties' commercial decisions. The agreement can then translate those decisions into enforceable rights, procedures, and remedies.
Identify the reseller, products, authorized customers, sales channels, and any prohibited activities.

Exclusivity can motivate a reseller to invest in sales staff, local marketing, training, or customer support. It can also limit the vendor's ability to sell directly or appoint stronger partners. The agreement should therefore define exactly what is exclusive. A territory may be geographic, but exclusivity can also apply to an industry, product line, customer class, or named accounts.

Agencies and offshore teams get the same treatment. A founder who says a team of 9 produced $3 million ARR, when 14 more people at an outsourced development shop built and maintain the product, has told a technically true story that won't survive a single follow-up question. Investors have seen it done, and they'll ask who writes the code.

Pair the metric with gross profit per employee. A reseller with a thin margin can post impressive revenue per head and have almost nothing left to pay the team. The investors who ask about revenue per employee are increasingly the same ones asking for gross margin rebuilt from invoices, so the two figures will be read together whether you present them that way or not.
